note: The Texas rain-enhancement programmes this evaluation is run against — the five TDLR lists at https://www.tdlr.texas.gov/weather/summary.htm. `releases` names the parsed flight record in this directory and `reports` the manifest of the region's 2025 documents, which `records.mjs` downloads into `cache/<id>/`. A region with an `origin` writes its positions as a bearing and a range from a point its reports do not name, and the note there says how that point was settled.

origin.name: the radar at Amarillo
origin.note: The flight tables give a bearing and a range and never say from where. Projected from Amarillo, 87% of the season's rows land inside the county their own row names; from the district office at White Deer, 9%. Whether the bearings are true or magnetic is not stated, and no rotation is applied: as printed, 76.5% of releases land in the county their row names, against 93.8% for West Texas and 96.1% for Trans-Pecos, the two programmes that print coordinates in one form all season. About 6° of eastward rotation closes most of that gap, which is what a magnetic display would mean — 4 km at 30 nm, under half a 12 km cell. South Texas projects its radials from an origin inferred the same way and wants about the same six degrees, which is the only corroboration there is. `registration.mjs` is where those figures come from.

origin.name: Pleasanton
origin.note: The flight tables print a bearing and a range from April on and never say from where. Projected from Pleasanton, the town the reports head themselves with, 76.9% of the season's radial rows land inside the county their own row names; from the municipal airport four kilometres south-west, 64.1%, and from San Antonio, Hondo or any of the three nearest radars, under 2%. Bearings are used as printed. About six degrees of eastward rotation raises the agreement to 89.7%, which is both what a magnetic display would look like and what a slightly misplaced origin would look like, and the reports say neither — the Panhandle, projected the same way from a different point by a different programme, wants about the same six degrees. `registration.mjs` is where those figures come from.

regions.name: Rolling Plains Water Enhancement Project
regions.note: Positions are read exactly as printed, and on three of the seven days that is demonstrably not decimal degrees. The reports write `32.69NX100.47W` in May and early June and `32.36, 100.38` on 30 June and 1 July, and the second form fits the county each row names only when its fractional part is read as minutes — 11 of 12 rows on 30 June land in the target area that way against 6 read as degrees. Nothing in the row says which it is, and a row whose fractions are both under .60 is a valid reading either way, so no notation is inferred and nothing is rewritten. The cost is that 58.5% of releases land in the county their own row names, against 94% and 96% for the two programmes that write coordinates one way all season. `registration.mjs` is where that figure comes from.
